scope.summary: Retire the legacy permanently-red backbone-microservices-ci GitHub Actions workflow from executable CI and preserve an inert audit copy.
explicit_non_claims: No required check is removed; the required context remains oya-ci-required.
No production deployment, application runtime, or backbone service source code changes are introduced.
No source Markdown files are introduced.

facets.F1_correctness: The legacy workflow is removed from .github/workflows so it cannot execute; an inert audit copy is retained under docs/audit/retired-workflows/.
facets.F2_tests: YAML parses as a data file; JSON/JSONL parse; generated faces are regenerated; registry-drift and gate-registration are the target local gates.
facets.F3_maintainability: Retirement reduces CI surface area to the single canonical oya-ci-required productized gate.
facets.F4_compatibility: Backbone service source files and manifests are untouched; only the obsolete CI lane location changes.
facets.F5_security: No credentials or privileged workflow permissions are introduced; executable GitHub Actions surface is reduced.
facets.F6_privacy: No tenant or personal data processing changes.
facets.F7_operability: Eliminates a known permanently-red non-required workflow that caused false operational noise.
facets.F8_performance: Reduces redundant CI spend by removing an obsolete matrix workflow.
facets.F9_compliance: Preserves audit history while enforcing the canonical required-check model.
facets.F10_reversibility: The inert audit copy can be restored only through a reviewed future change if product direction changes.
facets.F11_observability: Audit-chain and multispectrum evidence record the retirement decision.
facets.F13_migration: Supports Task #26 migration from legacy ad hoc CI lanes into cloud-ci/oya-ci required gates.

known_gaps: Reviewer approval remains pending; PR is not merged.
Full Task #26 migration of all retired oya-check/oya-dev-cli gates remains future backlog; this slice only removes the known permanently-red legacy backbone workflow.
